leading_positions.synthesis: Five of eight members name B046 (Katori, Ye; optical lattice clocks) as their preferred configuration. Shared: the magic-wavelength lattice idea plus a 1e-18-level realisation, independent reproduction at several national and university laboratories, new measurements (redshift over millimetres, constants, dark-matter searches), and the cleanest two-name credit on the shortlist. Not shared: how new it is relative to the 2005 comb prize and the 2012 prize on single quantum systems, whether Lemonde, Takamoto or Ludlow need a place, and whether to wait for the SI redefinition of the second. Some supporters (Johansson, Mehlig, Lindroth) moved to this position after reading the opening table; Kroll and Lindroth held it from first place. Kroll discloses proximity to the Ye group, and Pearce, Johansson and Mehlig all want the citation worded around the lattice invention rather than the comb.

Three members name B038 (Kane, Mele, Molenkamp; time-reversal-invariant topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect) as their preferred configuration. Shared: an original prediction followed by an original HgTe experiment, more than fifteen years of independent confirmation by transport and ARPES, and a new class of matter. Not shared: Eriksson and Olsson would keep the citation narrow to the 2D quantum spin Hall state, while Danielsson also stresses the broader reshaping of condensed-matter physics; all three accept that Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang (HgTe proposal) and the 3D contributors are a real attribution gap. All three list B046 among their alternatives; none rejects B046 on merit, and all three tie their preference to conceptual novelty versus attribution tidiness.

areas_of_agreement: Every member's preferred configuration is a single-part prize, and every one of the eight is either B046 or B038. No member's preferred configuration contains a second prize part.
B046 and B038 are each named as an alternative or an acknowledged strong competitor by members who prefer the other; no member argues that either lacks scientific merit.

Independent confirmation across laboratories is treated as the key maturity test, and both B046 (JILA, RIKEN/Tokyo, PTB, NIST, SYRTE) and B038 (HgTe, InAs/GaSb, Bi-based materials, ARPES) are described as meeting it.

Several members (Johansson, Lindroth, Kroll, Olsson, Pearce) say circuit QED (B006) has strong physics but its credit is unsettled (Blais versus Girvin for the theory slot, plus four claimants for three places) and its timing next to the 2025 prize is a concern.
A single-name IceCube prize (B025, Halzen) is seen as fragile by Pearce himself, who moved away from it, and by Danielsson, Lindroth and Johansson.
scientific_disputes: Discovery versus instrument: Danielsson, Eriksson and Olsson place a predicted and verified new state of matter (B038) above a precision-measurement invention (B046); Kroll, Lindroth, Mehlig and Pearce treat the lattice clock as a new way of observing nature, not only an engineering gain. Lindroth also notes that the instrument-versus-discovery distinction is the one she normally applies.

Whether the fundamental-physics payoff of lattice clocks (constants drift, dark matter, relativistic geodesy) consists so far of limits and demonstrations rather than findings (Danielsson, Kroll's own reservation).

Whether the 2016 prize on topological phases (Thouless, Haldane, Kosterlitz) makes B038 look like a second reward for the same theme: Danielsson and Eriksson argue the time-reversal-invariant Z2 class is distinct; Olsson, Lindroth, Mehlig and Kroll treat it as an open overlap question.
For the circuit QED candidate (B006), whether the recognised item is the strong-coupling physics or the processor platform (Kroll, Lindroth).

B036 (hexatic melting) is not universally confirmed (first-order melting in some systems) and abuts the 2016 prize; B042 (twisted bilayer graphene) lacks a settled pairing mechanism (Eriksson, Mehlig, Olsson).
attribution_disputes: B046: whether Lemonde (SYRTE), Takamoto, Ludlow, Hinkley or the ion-clock groups have claims that should alter or extend the Katori-Ye pair. Pearce and Lindroth lean towards a narrow citation around the invention; Kroll is more open to a third name. All priority history is stated as recalled from memory and not checked against the primary papers.

B038: Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang (HgTe quantum-well proposal that Molenkamp's experiment tested; Zhang deceased) and the 3D topological insulator contributors (Fu, Kane, Mele, Moore, Balents, Hasan) lie outside the three names. Olsson wants the gap stated openly; Eriksson asks how wide the citation should be; Danielsson asks for an expert account of Kane-Mele versus BHZ priority.
B006: Johansson's and Kroll's proposed trios differ (Blais versus Girvin alongside Schoelkopf and Wallraff), and Devoret-lineage transmon work sits near the 2025 laureates.

B017: Pearce proposed Bennett and Brassard for BB84 alone; Johansson disagrees and would include Ekert (E91, Bell-inequality basis, link to the 2022 prize), with Wiesner's earlier conjugate coding as a priority caveat.
B025: a sole Halzen credit for a collaboration of hundreds omits AMANDA and DUMAND pioneers (Pearce, Danielsson, Lindroth, Johansson).

Factual dispute: Olsson, Johansson, Lindroth, Mehlig and Pearce write that Ye shares the 2005 prize; Kroll recalls that the 2005 laureates were Glauber, Hall and Hansch and that Ye, as Hall's postdoc, was not a laureate. This is not settled in the eight files.
maturity_disputes: B046: whether to wait for the SI redefinition of the second (Olsson, who does not treat it as a veto) or act now (Kroll, Johansson, Lindroth, Mehlig, Pearce argue the science does not depend on a metrology-body timetable).
B038: the topological insulator is regarded as mature and timely by its supporters, while Olsson notes the experimental side rests on essentially one group for the first observation.
B042: whether a few more years would settle the superconducting mechanism and the credit (Eriksson, Mehlig, Danielsson).
B006: whether it should be held back for a later year given the 2025 prize on macroscopic quantum tunnelling in circuits (Johansson, Lindroth, Olsson, Pearce, Danielsson).
conflict_or_recusal_flags: Kroll (B046): doctoral period in John Hall's laboratory in Boulder; Ye is Hall's former postdoc and a JILA colleague, and his work on ultrastable laser stabilisation touches clock lasers; he flags possible recusal or at least disclosure. His WACQT role also overlaps institutionally with Chalmers and Johansson.

Johansson (B006, B033, B009): directs WACQT, works closely with Chalmers superconducting-circuit groups and has proximity to the 2025 laureates; says the member would recuse or declare on B006 and defer on B033 and B009. No link to Katori or Ye apparent.
Olsson: institutional proximity to Johansson at Chalmers and to Chalmers superconducting and device physics, so she would be cautious on B006; no recusal sought for B038.
Lindroth: long-standing collaboration with 2023 laureate Anne L'Huillier and mild proximity to ultracold-atom and attosecond groups (B009); no conflict on B046.

Pearce (B025): works in neighbouring cosmic-ray and gamma-ray collaborations (PAMELA, Fermi-LAT, XL-Calibur), so professional proximity to the IceCube community; no stated tie to Halzen. No conflict on B046 or B038.

Danielsson, Eriksson and Mehlig report no specific conflict; Eriksson declares a scientific bias towards topological-materials prediction, and Mehlig is in the Gothenburg physics environment near Chalmers colleagues.
questions_for_round2: B046 novelty: what, in one sentence, does a lattice-clock citation recognise that the 2005 frequency-comb prize and the 2012 prize on single quantum systems did not, and should it name magic-wavelength lattice trapping and its realisation explicitly?
Factual check: was Jun Ye a 2005 laureate or only a member of the Hall group? Members must agree on the record before the 2005 overlap argument is used for or against B046.
B046 attribution: do Lemonde, Takamoto or Ludlow have claims strong enough to alter or add to Katori and Ye, and if not, why not, given the three-person limit?

B038 attribution: can the condensed-matter members (Eriksson, Olsson, Danielsson) state a citation limited to the 2D quantum spin Hall state that is defensible without Bernevig, Hughes and Zhang, and does the 3D work need to be addressed or explicitly excluded?
B038 overlap: how does time-reversal-invariant Z2 band topology differ from the topological phases honoured in 2016, in terms the committee can write into a citation?

Decision between the two leaders: given that B046 has the cleaner credit and B038 the cleaner conceptual novelty, would B038 supporters accept B046 as the prize, and would B046 supporters accept B038, or is a two-part configuration under discussion?
Maturity of B046: should the pending SI redefinition of the second count for acting now, count for waiting, or be set aside as irrelevant to the science?
Recusal handling: should Kroll step back from, or only declare, his connection to Ye on B046, and should Johansson step back from B006, B033 and B009 if the committee turns to them?
summary.chair_observation: On the explicit round-1 configurations, five members prefer B046 and three prefer B038, with no other ballot preferred by any member. The two positions are separated less by merit than by how the committee weighs clean attribution and verified performance against conceptual novelty and the 2016 and 2005 overlap questions. Several priority claims are recalled from memory and one factual point (Ye and the 2005 prize) is contradicted among members, so round 2 should resolve those before the allocation is argued. The chair counts only what the eight files state.
